messages:
kyle: quick heads-up — noticed a 6% tail latency bump on host tokenization preparse during yesterday's high-qps canary (4k steady). p50 unchanged but p95/p99 up. @sophia can you take a look?
sophia: on it. which canary? link pls to the job.
kyle: canary id 2026-03-20T22:40, routed to hostpool-eu-west. attached sampling from perf (excerpt below). seems host-side CPU is skewed to parse/iter hotspots not kernel.
kyle: ```
perf top -p 12345
  31.7% token_parse_fastpath
  18.2% http2_frame_writev
  12.6% kv_cache_lookup_slow
   9.1% grpc_parse_slice
   5.4% memcpy
```
marcus: interesting — token_parse_fastpath is inlined path that uses kernel fingerprinting to select SIMD kernels. did kernel-selection metric change in the canary?
sophia: i rolled the kernel fingerprinting toggle on for that canary (kernel_probe=v2) to force new AVX path; defaults on prod are still v1.
simran: that would explain it. v2 uses a slightly different splitting heuristic that increases per-request parse calls (more branches). branch mispred + syscalls = tail.
kyle: exact hypothesis: the new kernel selection increases micro-batch fragmentation so KV cache hits drop (see kv_cache_lookup_slow). cache miss rate rose ~3.5% in sampling window.
anya: can we confirm by toggling kernel_probe back and re-run quick canary? also check batching window and batch-merge thresholds.
sophia: started a repro canary with kernel_probe=v1 + batching_window=6ms (was 3ms) to see if batching smoothing recovers tail. pinged deploy-bot to kick it off.
deploy-bot: canary 6555555590 queued -> running on hostpool-eu-west (kernel_probe=v1 batching_window=6ms). logs: https://ci.redwood.ai/canary/6555555590
marcus: also worth checking HTTP/2 small-write amplification. http2_frame_writev in perf suggests many tiny frames being writev-ed. we saw similar with grpc writev earlier — possible solution is coalesce at host-proxy before writev.\ksophia: (typo) sophia: yeah — we have a short-term shim that coalesces small frames on the proxy socket. it's off for canary due to earlier bug. re-enabling might help p99 while we tune kernel selection.
simran: can we add a microprobe that samples KV cache hit/miss per-token and kernel-id per request? would avoid full flame profiles. cheap counters aggregated every 1s.
anya: yes — i sketched a patch: incr counters {kernel_id, kv_hit, small_write_count} in preparse, emit to metrics sink every 1s. low overhead (atomic u64). will open PR.
kyle: metric payload idea: kernel_id=AVX2|AVX512|ref, kv_hit_ratio=0.962, small_write_rate=34/s. correlate with tail latency.
sophia: PR 4821 opened with counters + test. also added a simple synthetic that toggles kernel_probe and runs 5k synthetic requests to measure kv hit change.
sophia: initial synthetic numbers: kernel_probe=v2 => kv_hit 0.957, p95 decode + parse 32ms. kernel_probe=v1 => kv_hit 0.991, p95 26ms. exact numbers can change on infra but direction is clear.
marcus: good. i'd also like trace ids in the sample so we can backtrace full request if needed. add lightweight trace header capture (no spans).
simran: note: increasing batching_window reduces observed small writes but increases median tail at very low qps. need to auto-tune window by observed load (workload-aware).
anya: wrote a quick variant: batching_window = f(qps) where f clamps between 2ms-10ms and is smoothed with EWMA. will add to PR.
kyle: let's run three canaries in parallel: (A) kernel_probe=v1, batching_window=6ms, proxy_coalesce=on (B) kernel_probe=v2, batching_window=10ms, proxy_coalesce=on (C) kernel_probe=v2, batching_window=3ms, proxy_coalesce=off. compare p50/p95/p99 and kv_hit.
sophia: kicking them off now.
(deploy-bot): canary A -> 6555555595; canary B -> 6555555596; canary C -> 6555555597. dashboards: https://internal.redwood.ai/canaries/65555556xx
kyle: if A is clearly best, rollback v2 rollout and keep kernel_probe v1 while we improve v2 selection heuristics. we should also add a guard in the rollout to watch kv_hit ratio drop > 1% trigger rollback.
marcus: agreement. we should also add a smallwrite histogram to the SLA engine to catch regressions earlier.
sophia: after 10m: preliminary from canary A looks promising p95 down ~14% vs baseline, kv_hit +3.2%. B reduces small writes but p95 similar to baseline. C shows the worst tail.
simran: that matches hypothesis — kernel_probe v2 increases fragmentation; batching can mask but not fully fix.
anya: i'll iterate on kernel-selection: avoid re-splitting tokens if sequence-length < 64 and prefer fallback kernel. also plan to instrument branch-mispredict counters in next pass.
kyle: awesome. next steps: 1) promote canary A to extended run 2) add kv_hit rollback trigger + smallwrite metric to SLA 3) land probe counters and batching EWMA.
sophia: noted. i'll open followups for the rollback guard and SLA metric.
marcus: thanks team. can we sync in 30m to review extended canary results? :thumbsup:
kyle: yep. meeting in 30.
